## RosettaGBR: translation between methods for measuring COTS and coral cover on the Great Barrier Reef

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/dangladish/RosettaGBR/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dangladish/RosettaGBR/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

## Summary

RosettaGBR is an R package that provides the results of a calibration exercise between different methods for measuring Crown-of-Thorns Starfish (COTS) and coral cover on the Great Barrier Reef (GBR). Its main function `GBR_calibrate` is a tool that predicts one measure from another, along with confidence and prediction intervals. Two further functions help with analysing the results: `GBR_curve` returns the whole calibration curve for a pair of tools, and `GBR_posterior` returns the fitted posterior draws. RosettaGBR is built upon data obtained during 2025/2026 Reef Joint Field Management Program (RJFMP) trips, and extends [RosettaCOTS](https://github.com/Scott-Foster/RosettaCOTS), which presents the site-level calibration models from the CCIP D-02 field trip. Where RosettaCOTS works at the site level, RosettaGBR works at three spatial levels: the individual manta tow, the cull site and the reef. It presents the results of the pair-wise models of the methods that measure COTS and of the methods that measure coral cover. The fitted models are bundled with the package.

The COTS measurement methods are:

* Manta Tow (`Manta`): the number of COTS seen on each tow, and a feeding-scar code for each tow (absent, present or common). Used together, as a combined density of COTS plus tows with scars.
* ReefScan Surface (`ReefScan_surface`): COTS detected in images taken from a camera system towed behind the vessel (the "Transom"). Effort is the number of tows.
* ReefScan Deep (`ReefScan_deep`): as ReefScan Surface, except that images were taken using a different measurement platform.
* eDNA concentration (`eDNA_conc`): the concentration (quantitative measure) from each PCR assay. There is a hierarchy to this sampling: multiple samples at a reef, and replicate assays on each sample.
* eDNA proportion (`eDNA_prop`): as eDNA concentration, except that the measure is dichotomous (presence/absence of COTS eDNA in a sample). This is accumulated to the reef by taking the proportion of positive samples.

The coral cover measurement methods are:

* Manta Tow (`coral_manta`): an ordinal hard coral cover category for each tow, converted to the category midpoint.
* ReefScan Surface (`coral_surface`): the proportion of classified image points that are hard coral.
* ReefScan Deep (`coral_deep`): as ReefScan Surface, except that images were taken using a different measurement platform.

The tool names are the values used for the `from` and `to` arguments. Predictions can only be made within COTS measurements and within coral measurements. The models are Beta regression (coral cover), Negative Binomial regression (COTS counts) and Binomial regression (COTS presence/absence), with reef included as a random effect where the data allow. Every pair is modelled in both directions. How to use the package is illustrated further below. Note that this README is performing a similar role to that of a vignette (so there is no vignette).

### Installation

The `RosettaGBR` package can be installed using the `remotes` (or `devtools`) R package.

```r
install.packages('remotes')
remotes::install_github(repo = "dangladish/RosettaGBR")
```

## Which pairs are available

Every pair of tools exists at reef level. Cull-site and tow level exist for the manta tow and ReefScan tools but not for eDNA, which is only sampled at the reef. Predicting a manta COTS *count* is possible from the ReefScan tools only; predicting manta *presence* is possible from every COTS tool.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
reg <- RosettaGBR:::loadRegistry()
nm <- c(manta = "Manta", rs_surface = "ReefScan_surface", rs_deep = "ReefScan_deep", edna_conc = "eDNA_conc", edna_prop = "eDNA_prop")
cots <- reg[reg$family != "beta", ]
tab <- aggregate(level ~ predictor_method + response_method, cots,
                 function(l) paste(c("tow", "cull_site", "reef")[c("tow", "cull_site", "reef") %in% l], collapse = ", "))
tab <- data.frame(from = nm[tab$predictor_method], to = nm[tab$response_method], levels = tab$level, row.names = NULL)
knitr::kable(tab[order(tab$from, tab$to), ], row.names = FALSE, caption = "COTS pairs and the levels at which they are available.")
```

The three coral cover tools (`coral_manta`, `coral_surface`, `coral_deep`) can each be predicted from either of the other two, at tow, cull-site and reef level.

## Using the package

The main function is `GBR_calibrate`. You give it the observations from the `from` tool in the units they are normally recorded in, a label for the site each observation belongs to, and the tool you want to predict. It returns one row per site, with a summary of your input data, the effort assumed for the prediction, the predicted value, a confidence interval (how far the mean prediction may vary) and a prediction interval (how far a new observation may vary). The `level` argument says whether observations are tows, or are combined within cull sites or reefs.

### Coral cover

Here we predict what manta tow coral cover would be at two reefs, given ReefScan Surface cover (proportions) from several tows at each.

```{r}
library(RosettaGBR)
set.seed(7416)

surf <- data.frame(
  reef  = rep(c("reefA", "reefB"), each = 5),
  cover = c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.12, 0.18, 0.40, 0.45, 0.35, 0.50, 0.42)
)

GBR_calibrate(
  from = "coral_surface", to = "coral_manta", level = "reef",
  from.metric = surf$cover, sites = surf$reef
)
```

The manta tow categories can be supplied as they are recorded (`"0"`, `"1-"`, `"1+"`, ..., `"5+"`) and are converted to their midpoints.

### COTS from manta tows

Manta tows need the COTS seen on each tow (`from.metric`) and the feeding-scar code of each tow (`from.scars`: `"a"`, `"p"` or `"c"`). Here we predict the number of COTS that ReefScan Surface would detect over 27 tows (the median number of tows at a reef in the BR-04 data, and the default) at two reefs.

```{r}
manta <- data.frame(
  reef  = rep(c("reefA", "reefB"), each = 6),
  cots  = c(0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 1, 0, 3, 1),
  scars = c("a", "a", "p", "a", "a", "a", "p", "p", "p", "a", "c", "p")
)

GBR_calibrate(
  from = "Manta", to = "ReefScan_surface", level = "reef",
  from.metric = manta$cots, from.scars = manta$scars, sites = manta$reef
)
```

The effort assumed in the prediction can be changed with `to.nTows` (for a cull site or reef), so that a prediction for 10 tows is

```{r}
GBR_calibrate(
  from = "Manta", to = "ReefScan_surface", level = "reef",
  from.metric = manta$cots, from.scars = manta$scars, sites = manta$reef,
  to.nTows = 10
)
```

### Predicting manta tows

When the manta tow is the tool being predicted, there are two kinds of prediction, chosen by `to.type`. The default, `"presence"`, is the probability that a tow has a scar present or at least one COTS seen (at cull-site and reef level, the proportion of `to.nTows` tows that do). The alternative, `"count"`, is the combined COTS-plus-scar count, and is only available from the ReefScan tools. At tow level the effort is the tow distance in metres (`to.effort`).

```{r}
# eDNA detections (0/1) for the 24 samples taken at a reef
detections <- c(rep(1, 6), rep(0, 18))

GBR_calibrate(
  from = "eDNA_prop", to = "Manta", level = "reef",
  from.metric = detections, sites = rep("reefA", length(detections)),
  to.type = "presence"
)

# Tow level: one row per tow, ReefScan Surface counts from three tows
GBR_calibrate(
  from = "ReefScan_surface", to = "Manta", level = "tow",
  from.metric = c(0, 1, 3), to.type = "count", to.effort = 200
)
```

### eDNA

For `eDNA_conc`, `from.metric` is the concentration of each PCR assay, and the predictor is the total concentration per assay. When `eDNA_conc` is the tool being predicted, the prediction is the total concentration over `to.effort` assays (default 48). For `eDNA_prop` it is a proportion of `to.effort` samples (default 24). Both exist at reef level only.

## Calibration curves

`GBR_curve` returns the whole calibration curve for a pair of tools rather than predictions for particular observations: the expected value of the `to` tool over a grid of values of the `from` tool, with confidence and prediction intervals. It uses the same tool names, levels, `to.type`, `to.nTows` and `to.effort` as `GBR_calibrate`. The result is an ordinary data frame, ready for `ggplot2` or any other plotting tool, and it has a `plot` method that draws the mean, the confidence band and the prediction band. The mean line is dashed where the curve is an extrapolation beyond the range of the predictor in the BR-04 data (the `observed` column).

```{r curve, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
set.seed(2931)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# How manta tow coral cover relates to ReefScan Surface cover, by reef
cover_curve <- GBR_curve(from = "coral_surface", to = "coral_manta", level = "reef")
plot(cover_curve)

# Chance that a manta tow finds COTS or scars, as ReefScan Surface density rises
cots_curve <- GBR_curve(from = "ReefScan_surface", to = "Manta", level = "tow")
plot(cots_curve)
```

```{r}
head(cots_curve)
```

The axis labels are kept with the curve, so the scale of `x` and of the prediction is always recorded.

```{r}
attr(cots_curve, "xlab")
attr(cots_curve, "ylab")
```

You can give your own grid of predictor values with `x`, and the `x` scale is the one the models were fitted on: a proportion for coral cover and `eDNA_prop`, COTS per tow for the ReefScan tools, the combined density for `Manta` (COTS seen plus tows with scars, per tow), and the concentration per assay for `eDNA_conc`. Overlaying your own observations is then a matter of adding points to the plot.

## Posterior draws

`GBR_posterior` returns the fitted posterior draws behind a pair of tools, as an ordinary data frame with one row per draw. No Bayesian software is needed to use them. The draws are for the average reef (group effects are set to zero).

```{r}
draws <- GBR_posterior(from = "coral_surface", to = "coral_manta", level = "reef")
head(draws)
```

The `model_info` attribute says which model it is and how the parameters combine:

```{r}
attr(draws, "model_info")$equation
```

A one-row-per-parameter summary is available with `summary = TRUE`:

```{r}
GBR_posterior(from = "Manta", to = "ReefScan_surface", level = "reef", summary = TRUE)
```

and the draws can be used for your own calculations. For example, the posterior distribution of manta tow coral cover when ReefScan Surface cover is 30%:

```{r}
info <- attr(draws, "model_info")
eta <- draws$alpha + draws$beta * 0.3
mu <- if (info$link == "loglog") exp(-exp(-eta)) else plogis(eta)
quantile(mu, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
```

The parameters are `alpha` and `beta` for every model, plus `phi` (Beta precision, coral cover models), `r` (Negative Binomial size, COTS count models), and `obs_re_sd` (the standard deviation of an observation-level reef effect, reef-level presence models). See `?GBR_posterior` for details.

### Intervals and randomness

The confidence and prediction intervals are 95% unless `intLevel` says otherwise. Predictions are for the average reef. The prediction intervals are simulated, so use `set.seed()` first if you need reproducible numbers. Some pairs involving ReefScan Deep rest on very few reefs; `GBR_calibrate` prints a message when such a model is used, and these should be treated as exploratory.

See `?GBR_calibrate`, `?GBR_curve` and `?GBR_posterior` for the full list of arguments and the units each tool expects.

## Funding

This package is an output of the COTS Control and Innovation Program (CCIP) project BR-04 (Analysing RJFMP Data), which builds on the CCIP `Tool Comparison' project (D-02).

## Contributing Software

Fork the `RosettaGBR` repository

Clone your fork using the command:

`git clone https://github.com/<username>/RosettaGBR.git`

Contribute to your forked repository.

Create a pull request.

If your code passes the necessary checks and is documented, your changes and/or additions will be merged in the main `RosettaGBR` repository.

## Reporting Bugs

If you notice an issue with this repository, please report it using [Github Issues](https://github.com/dangladish/RosettaGBR/issues). When reporting an implementation bug, include a small example that helps to reproduce the error (a non-working minimal example). The issue will be addressed as quickly as possible.

## Seeking Support

If you have questions or need additional support, please open a [Github Issues](https://github.com/dangladish/RosettaGBR/issues).
